openQuestions: Word image export is built on the PDF writer+reader+renderer (WordPageImageExport). Keeping image export in OfficeIMO.Word without the PDF engine requires splitting OfficeIMO.Pdf into a composition/pagination core that paints to OfficeIMO.Drawing (Core) and a PDF writer. That is a large engine refactor; the cheaper option is to move Word image export to OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf (or a new OfficeIMO.Word.Imaging that references Pdf) and accept that Word image export needs the PDF engine. PowerPoint does not have this problem (its scene renderer already targets OfficeIMO.Drawing).

Dropping the Windows-only net472 TFM means .NET Framework consumers run the netstandard2.0 build. #if NETFRAMEWORK workarounds (Word Save snapshot, Excel non-seekable stream save, PDF NET472 branches) must become runtime checks, and the netstandard2.0 build must be tested on .NET Framework 4.7.2 (PSWriteOffice on Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the main consumer).
WordDocument.ToMarkdown() string -> MarkdownDocument (Word.Markdown) changes the return type of a widely used call; consider whether the string form keeps a name (ToMarkdownText).

packageMoves.notes: The design keeps image export in the format package only on its own rendering code. Word has no own paginating layout: pagination and line breaking are done by the PDF composition engine (PdfParagraphBuilder, PdfTableStyle, PdfPageBuilder: 193 PdfCore references across Layout/). A lower-level shared package would have to split OfficeIMO.Pdf into a composition/pagination core that paints to OfficeIMO.Drawing (Core) plus the PDF writer/reader. Until that split exists, the honest placement is the adapter.

Specialized static content-safety, provenance and signature inspection entry points are internal native kernels. OfficeDocument.Inspect(path, OfficeInspectOptions) returns OfficeDocumentInfo with selectable typed reports and optional native content. IncludeContent=false preserves inspection without content extraction; original package/signature/provenance guards and explicit provider selection remain in their owning libraries. Provenance takes an independent options snapshot with caller cancellation.

Password-bearing Load retains the requested SaveOnDispose lifecycle while decoding into a private package with explicit persistence. Disposal writes only through the associated encrypted destination. Native fallback fixtures inject the Word.Pdf visual renderer explicitly at the internal conversion boundary.

The existing OfficeChartSeries model becomes root OfficeIMO.OfficeSeries, adding numeric typed-selector factories. OfficeChartKind merges into the M1 OfficeChartType enum. Native chart writers and all in-repo type consumers use that single enum/model; typed and nameof-based AddChart overloads reuse the existing shared native chart data pipeline. Core builds on all three macOS targets with zero warnings; six typed native chart artifact cases and 166 shared chart regression cases pass on each modern framework.

The shared declared-schema projection handles public properties, fields and string-keyed dictionaries without arbitrary object graph reflection. Word also retains rectangular text/matrix input and an explicit dynamic-object overload; PowerPoint retains configurable object flattening with an explicit configure argument; Excel retains DataTable values and returns native ExcelTable wrappers. Focused authoring tests: 10/10 per modern target; final table signature check: 4/4 per target.

extraChanges.change: Preserve native Word authoring after fluent removal
extraChanges.note: OfficeCalloutKind is shared in Core. Word has document-local code styles, optional TOC title/top placement, task/link list items, a NumberFormat list-level property, and zero-based logical table insertion. AddImage returns WordImage and its Paragraph identifies the containing run; WordImageOptions carries metadata, placement, hyperlink and maximum width. The existing embedded image reading methods remain. Image geometry, VML/resource/base64/URL consolidation and the remaining Add returns are separate pending map entries. Twelve builder-only test files and two duplicate builder-specific methods are removed; meaningful mutation, crop, regex, and conversion proof uses native objects.

WordImageOptions adds Vml. Header and section AddImage delegate to the paragraph owner; paragraph, document, header and section VML entry points merge into AddImage options. Async insertion snapshots image metadata before awaiting the shared bounded HTTP loader. The async overload also accepts image metadata options in addition to the shared network policy, preserving the capabilities of the removed image builder.

Package README and maintained website examples now use native document/table authoring and caller-owned image streams. The obsolete reflection test that pinned the removed Word image builder is removed; image relationship, resource, remote-load, VML and conversion artifact tests retain the behavior coverage. All changed in-repo image consumers use OfficeLength and WordImageOptions, including mechanical PSWriteOffice argument conversion without changing PowerShell parameters.
Typed AddTable applies shared selection, order, header transformation, formatting and column alignment.

Document, section and header/footer forwarding entry points and native static field, bookmark and hyperlink helpers return their created models. WordField, WordBookmark, WordHyperLink, WordEquation, WordEmbeddedObject, WordFootNote and WordEndNote expose the containing Paragraph. Fields and note references retain the exact newly attached native elements when several objects share a paragraph.

Comment creation supports empty paragraphs and paragraphs containing hyperlinks without a direct run. Range markers enclose the paragraph content and references follow the range end. WordTable.AddComment rejects a table without cells before creating a comment.

Native consumers, adapters, examples, tests and the Word README use the created models. Mechanical PowerShell changes explicitly select Paragraph where existing cmdlet output requires it; command parameters and output contracts are preserved.

WordSmartArtNode.Id addresses a native node independently of its index. WordSmartArt.Nodes exposes attached handles in diagram order; edits reuse the existing node text and package-part writers. Removed nodes reject subsequent reads and writes instead of editing a different node at the former index.
